title: A generic stalk detects kernels in a locally constant sheaf
statement:
Let $S$ be a nonempty irreducible scheme with generic point $\eta$, and fix a
geometric point $\bar\eta$ over $\eta$. Let $F$ be a locally constant abelian
etale sheaf, let $G$ be any abelian etale sheaf, and let $\phi:F\to G$ be a
morphism. If $\phi_{\bar\eta}$ is injective, then $\phi$ is a monomorphism.

proof.text: It suffices by Abelian.mono_of_kernel_ι_eq_zero to show kernel.ι φ=0. If this inclusion were nonzero, apply the local nonzero-germ theorem to N=kernel φ, F, and ψ=kernel.ι φ. Obtain a nonempty etale neighbourhood U and a section s of the kernel whose image has nonzero germ at every geometric point with a lift to U.

The image of U.hom is open by Mathlib UniversallyOpen.of_flat and Scheme.Hom.isOpenMap, since an etale map is flat and locally of finite presentation. The image is nonempty, so IsGenericPoint.mem_open_set_iff shows it contains η. Choose w over η. Mathlib Scheme.pointSmallEtaleFiberObjToPreimage_surjective applied to barη and w gives a pointed lift t∈(pointSmallEtale barη).fiber.obj U.

Applying the generic stalk functor to kernel.condition gives stalk(kernel.ι φ)≫stalk(φ)=0. Cancel the monic stalk(φ) to conclude stalk(kernel.ι φ)=0. Naturality of toPresheafFiber then makes the germ of the image of s equal to zero. This contradicts the nonzero germ assertion at Ω,barη,t. Hence kernel.ι φ=0 and φ is mono. This only uses preservation of zero morphisms, not a kernel comparison or full exactness of stalks.
